title: Choose the visual world for arpitkhandelwal.com
question: The roll assigned The Patent Specification. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Patent Specification
options.lineage: patent drawings and specifications: FIG. sheets, reference numerals, claims
options.thesis: Every build is filed as an invention: a drawn figure, numbered parts, and claims that resolve to live links.
materials: black ink line art on bond
options.viewport: Sheet 1 of N: a full-width FIG. 1 drawing of how an agent, a closed app and a backend get wired, with the title block naming Arpit, and the abstract plus the live brief action set into the sheet margin.
options.risk: Goes dry and grey if the figures are timid; the drawings have to be big, dense and funny.

raised.raise: Every claim carries a reference numeral that resolves to a live artifact: a URL, a merged PR, a repo.
The audience switch re-letters the same sheet (abstract and claims rewrite per reader) instead of swapping a hero.
The sprint brief is a blank application form whose empty fields read as invitation, not a contact form.
FIG. 0 shows this very page as an agent reads it: the markdown twin and llms.txt as a drawn figure.
Every figure interaction is mirrored in the text: hover or focus a numeral and its part lights, both ways.

options.label: The Laptop Lid
options.thesis: The archive is a laptop lid covered in die-cut stickers, one per build; peel one to read the case.
options.viewport: The lid fills the viewport, 30+ stickers overlapping at real scale, the name on a hackathon badge sticker.
options.risk: The most familiar dev-culture trope here; can read as cute rather than senior.

options.label: The Title Wall
options.thesis: Builds as rows of title cards (Shipped, Experiments, Open source) that grow when focused.
materials: full-bleed screenshots of the live builds
options.viewport: A featured build fills the top, rows of real screenshots below, metadata only on the focused tile.
options.case: Everyone reads it instantly and it browses a 25-build archive well; it loses on showing how he wires systems.
options.risk: Netflix-portfolio is a known gimmick and the dark ground edges toward the neon default.

options.label: Sliding House
options.thesis: One room re-partitioned per visitor by sliding primary planes.
options.viewport: Four planes, one per audience, slide to reconfigure the page.
options.case: Clever fit for the audience switch, but founders and recruiters don't identify with De Stijl, and it says nothing about the work.
options.kept: Re-partition the same sheet per reader instead of swapping pages.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Forces traced from load to counterforce.
options.viewport: A breathing column annotated with force values.
options.case: Same drawing family as the roll with less identification and less room for the archive.
options.kept: Every claim traceable to its proof.

options.label: Step Row
options.thesis: The sprint as sixteen lit steps under a chase light.
options.viewport: A sixteen-step sprint row with a tempo readout.
options.case: Charming for the sprint loop, too thin for the archive and the four audiences.
options.kept: An empty pattern is an invitation: blank fields that ask to be filled.

options.label: Source Floor
options.viewport: A live code buffer at stage scale.
options.case: A terminal costume on the near-black-plus-neon default; the incumbent's own trap.
options.kept: Show the page's own source: the agent-readable twin as part of the page.

options.label: Alphabet Storm
options.thesis: Letters condense into words and break into weather.
options.viewport: A word storm over white ground.
options.case: /play already does letters-as-matter; as a whole site it hides every fact.
options.kept: Transformations stay reversible and narrated in text.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The engineer portfolio every visitor expects, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Name and one-line role, a headshot, then a grid of project cards and a contact link.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other engineer's site by design.
